app.name: Muzdyq
app.tagline: An open time series of the Ile Alatau
app.subtitle: Repeat photos of glaciers and water bodies, made by people who walk there.

hero.title: The mountains are changing. Help us keep watch.
hero.body: Photograph the same viewpoint every time you hike. Your photos become an open, reusable time series of the glaciers and lakes that supply Almaty and foothill villages.
hero.meta: No account. No tracking. Works offline.

steps.title: Three small steps
steps.subtitle: A useful observation takes less than a minute.

one.title: Choose a viewpoint
one.body: Every point has a fixed reference frame. You do not need to find a new angle or climb somewhere risky.

two.title: Align and shoot
two.body: Hold your phone where the ghost image lines up, then take one photo.

three.title: Save — we do the rest
three.body: The photo is compressed, stripped of location data and queued. It uploads when you get signal.

about.title: About Muzdyq
about.lead: Muzdyq (“glacial” in Kazakh) is an open, account-free way to build a public photo time series of the glaciers, lakes and rivers of the Ile Alatau.
about.problem: The glaciers of the Ile Alatau feed Almaty and foothill villages. Scientific monitoring is intensive on a few glaciers, such as Tuyuksu, but many historical photo series stopped in the 1990s. Researchers need regular, comparable images. Hikers and locals pass these places every week.
about.mission: Fix a small number of safe viewpoints. Give each one a reference frame. Ask visitors for one aligned photo, with no account and no location tracking. Publish the result openly so anyone can reuse it.
about.scienceTitle: What these photos can and cannot tell us
about.science: Repeat photos show visible changes: snowline, ice margins, lake colour, debris cover and infrastructure. They are observations, not measurements. They cannot replace mass-balance studies, ground surveys or satellite analysis. Conclusions about glacier state require verification by scientists.
about.sdg13body: Climate education, awareness and institutional capacity. Every photo page shows what is changing and why it matters, with a clear scientific caveat.
about.sdg66body: Protect and restore water-related ecosystems. The series covers glacier-fed lakes and rivers as well as ice, with open data for local researchers and teachers.
about.dpgBody: Muzdyq is designed against the Digital Public Goods Standard: open licence, open data, platform independence, privacy by design, do-no-harm and documentation. The repository maps each indicator to evidence in docs/DPG_CHECKLIST.md.
about.openBody: Code is MIT-licensed. Photo data and metadata are CC BY 4.0. Exports work without authentication in CSV, GeoJSON, JSON and ZIP. No analytics trackers, no third-party cookies and no mandatory accounts.
about.usersBody: Hikers and tourists are the primary contributors. Glaciologists, teachers, eco-activists and journalists reuse the data. The interface is built for weak connectivity, small screens, bright sunlight and people who do not want another account.
about.faq1a: No. There is no sign-up or login anywhere. Photos are uploaded anonymously with an idempotency key, so a retry does not create a duplicate.
about.faq2a: No. EXIF and GPS are removed on your device and again on the server. The map shows only the fixed monitoring point, never your phone's position.
about.faq3q: Can I upload from any angle?
about.faq3a: Photos are only accepted for predefined viewpoints. The ghost overlay helps you match the reference frame.
about.faq4q: Is this a glacier monitoring service?
about.faq4a: No. It is a citizen-science photo archive. Images support education and research, but they are not measurements and must be verified by scientists.
about.faq5a: No ratings, leaderboards, badges or streaks. Nothing should encourage anyone to take a risk for a photo.
about.contactBody: Open an issue in the repository for corrections, new viewpoints or data questions. Coordinate verification with glaciologists is required before a point is marked verified.

data.title: Data & API
data.lead: Every published observation is open data. Download it, query it, teach with it, or build on it — no key, no account.
data.licenseBody: Photo data and metadata are licensed CC BY 4.0. The code is MIT. You may share and adapt the data for any purpose, including commercially, as long as you give appropriate credit and indicate changes. Attribution: “Muzdyq Citizen Science Photo Archive, CC BY 4.0”.
data.downloadsBody: Exports include only published photos. Demo images are marked is_demo=true. Coordinates are the fixed monitoring point, not the photographer.
data.apiBody: The FastAPI service documents itself at /docs. Public read and export endpoints need no authentication.
data.noAuth: No API key. No account. No contributor login.
data.rateLimit: Upload rate limits protect the service. Exports are open.
data.schemaBody: Each photo record includes the following public fields.

notes.id: Client-generated idempotency UUID for uploads; stable photo id in the archive.
notes.point_slug: Link to the fixed monitoring point.
notes.taken_at: Capture time supplied by the client, rounded down to the hour. Never read from EXIF.
notes.width_height: Pixel dimensions after server downscaling and re-encoding.
notes.tags: Whitelisted weather, visibility and snow-cover values. No free text.
notes.phash: Perceptual hash used for duplicate detection and research.
notes.url: Image and thumbnail endpoints. ZIP bundles include originals.
notes.coordinates: Hardcoded viewpoint coordinates only. Device GPS is never stored.

data.attributionBody: Credit “Muzdyq Citizen Science Photo Archive, CC BY 4.0”, link to the licence, and indicate if you changed the data. Do not imply that Muzdyq or its contributors endorse your use.
data.scienceBody: Citizen photos are observations, not measurements. Conclusions about glacier state require verification by scientists. Cite the export date and the specific observation timestamps.
data.contactBody: Found an error, a mislabelled point or a privacy problem? Open an issue or use the moderation contact in the repository.

ethics.title: Ethics & privacy
ethics.lead: Muzdyq is built around data minimisation, physical safety and scientific honesty. No contributor account exists, because we never need to identify you.
ethics.safetyBody: Every capture screen repeats the safety note. Photos are only accepted from predefined viewpoints. There are no ratings, leaderboards, badges or streaks that could push someone into a dangerous place.
ethics.collected: The photo itself, the fixed point and viewpoint, capture time rounded to the hour, upload time, optional weather/visibility/snow tags, dimensions, file size, a perceptual hash, a salted hash of the IP address and an anonymous device token. Published records are public.
ethics.notCollectedTitle: What is never stored or published
ethics.notCollected: Your name, email, phone number, account, raw IP address, device GPS, EXIF metadata, free-text notes, advertising identifiers or third-party analytics. Live camera frames are never sent to the server.
ethics.exifBody: The browser re-encodes the image through a canvas to strip EXIF before it enters the offline queue. The server validates the bytes, strips EXIF again, applies orientation and re-encodes. Only the hardcoded monitoring point is public.
ethics.faceBody: The server detects faces with OpenCV YuNet and blurs each detected region before publication. The client attempts the same on supported browsers. If you can still identify a person in a published photo, report it and we will hide it promptly.
ethics.noGamificationBody: No likes, scores, rankings, streaks, badges or collection mechanics. The only number shown is how many observations exist for a point.
ethics.analyticsBody: The app uses no analytics, advertising or social embeds. Map tiles are loaded from OpenStreetMap only when you open the map; their requests are subject to OSM's policies. Prefer the offline tile download when possible.
ethics.moderationBody: Automated checks strip metadata, blur faces, enforce size limits and detect near-duplicates. A token-protected admin endpoint can hide or remove a photo. There is no public uploader identity to ban.
ethics.accessibilityBody: Targets WCAG 2.1 AA: large tap targets, strong contrast, keyboard support, screen-reader labels, 360 px layouts and reduced-motion support. Report an accessibility barrier in the repository.
ethics.doNoHarmBody: No viewpoint is placed on unsafe terrain. Coordinates are marked unverified until glaciologists and local guides confirm them. The platform does not name sensitive sites, publish routes or encourage off-trail access.
ethics.retentionBody: Published photos stay in the archive. Hidden photos are excluded from public endpoints. IP and device hashes are operational abuse signals and should be purged after 180 days; the backend includes a maintenance command for this.
ethics.contactBody: For privacy, safety or moderation requests, open a confidential security report as described in SECURITY.md or contact the maintainers listed in the repository. We aim to respond within seven days.

contribute.title: Contribute a photo
contribute.lead: One aligned photo from a safe viewpoint is enough. No account, no app store, no special equipment.
contribute.beforeBody: Check the weather and trail conditions. Carry water, warm layers and a charged phone. Tell someone your route. A photo is never worth leaving the marked trail.
contribute.step1: Open the map and choose a monitoring point near your route.
contribute.step2: Tap “Add photo” and allow camera access, or choose a photo from your device.
contribute.step3: Line up the reference ghost image. Match the ridge line and the main rock or building.
contribute.step4: Add optional weather and snow tags, save, and upload when you have signal.
contribute.safetyBody: Glacier ice, snow bridges and moraine edges can collapse. Weather changes quickly. Never enter closed areas or cross barriers. In an emergency call 112 in Kazakhstan.
contribute.standsBody: Each viewpoint has a QR link that opens the capture flow directly. You can print a small sign for a trail stand. Use only durable, removable fixings.
contribute.qrCaption: This QR code opens the capture flow for {{viewpoint}}.
contribute.printHint: Print at A5, laminate, and fix securely beside the trail. Never drill into rock, attach to living trees or block the path.
contribute.codeBody: The code is MIT-licensed. Issues, translations, accessibility fixes, tests and documentation improvements are welcome. Read CONTRIBUTING.md and the Code of Conduct before opening a pull request.
contribute.translateBody: Kazakh, Russian and English interfaces live in the frontend i18n files. Improve a translation without touching any code logic.
contribute.dataBody: Researchers and teachers can download CSV, GeoJSON, JSON or a ZIP of images without authentication. Please preserve the CC BY 4.0 attribution.
contribute.noAccounts: There is no sign-up, login, leaderboard or badge. Contribution is anonymous by design.
contribute.contactBody: Open an issue in the repository to propose a new viewpoint, report a broken QR sign or ask about the data.
